The graph represents the function $y=\frac{a}{x-b}+k.$ What are the values of $a,$ $b,$ and $k?$

$a=$
{{field-1}},$\,b=$
{{field-2}},$\,k=$
{{field-3}}
worked_solution:
First, notice that the horizontal asymptote of the graph is $y=2.5,$ while the vertical asymptote is $x=-2.$ This means that $k=2.5$ and $b=-2,$ and we can re-write our function as

$$
y=\frac{a}{x-(-2)}+2.5=\frac{a}{x+2}+2.5.
$$

Also, we are given that the point $(-5,3.5)$ lies on the graph. Substituting its coordinates into the equation above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{a}{x+2}+2.5 \\ 3.5 & =\frac{a}{-5+2}+2.5 \\ 1 & =\frac{a}{(-3)} \\ a & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$
